cases.prompt: Our Go HTTP pod exits while requests are active. Review main, Server.Shutdown, readiness, and WebSocket handling.
cases.reason: The failure is at the HTTP lifecycle boundary.

cases.prompt: An outbound net/http client exhausts connections under error responses. Check response-body and timeout handling.
cases.reason: The task concerns client resource ownership and pooling.

cases.prompt: Design gRPC unary interceptors and status-code mapping for this Go service.
cases.reason: The transport is not HTTP through net/http semantics.

cases.prompt: Choose field names and pagination schema for our REST resource.
cases.reason: This is API contract design, not HTTP resource-boundary behavior.

cases.prompt: Add recommended timeouts to a Go server with normal JSON routes and an hour-long server-sent-events endpoint.
criteria: Rejects one universal write timeout for incompatible route semantics.
Bounds header and finite-body behavior while preserving healthy streaming.
Explains how the streaming endpoint terminates during shutdown.
anti_criteria: Copies the same read and write timeout to every route without analysis.
Claims Server.Shutdown waits for every upgraded or hijacked connection.

cases.prompt: A peer returns a 4 GB error body. Should the Go client always io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body) so the connection can be reused?
criteria: Requires closing the body and bounding any optional drain.
Frames connection reuse as a trade-off against bandwidth and trust.
anti_criteria: Reads the entire response solely for reuse.
